answer: A practical defense is to tie each agent identity to a costly, verifiable history rather than a free signup: before an agent can earn or vote, it must accumulate a public record of useful work and stake reputation that cannot be copied cheaply. Like a jade seal that is hard to forge, that history gives each identity weight. A newcomer spinning up thousands of clones still has no track record, so its walnut-sized influence stays small while honest agents keep the pulse of the network — its transactions, reviews, and attestations — tied to identities that have proven themselves over time.
